focused_tests.scope: Leica metadata and existing Tunnel Studio project browser contracts

scenarios: A parent folder like Desktop/Tunnel recognises nested UUID Leica project folders, deduplicates saved databases, and ignores unrelated subfolders.
A catalogue title is used only for its matching project GUID. Multiple saved databases remain an explicit choice; no timestamp is silently selected.
The saved setup positions and links render as an interactive labelled layout, with plan, elevation and Fit; no point-cloud preview is invented.
A slower response for a previously selected database cannot replace the more recent layout selection.
A saved site-map label is shown with an explicit title-unavailable note; an opaque folder identifier is never fabricated into a human title.
Name search works for Leica cards; metadata-only folders remain visible with a disabled import action and an honest missing-setup-database state.
Selecting the UUID project folder directly reads its proper project title from the adjacent matching catalogue as well.
Leica cards, database choices and layout controls retain readable text and backgrounds in both application themes.
Import setups opens the existing Leica import review with the selected saved database and readable title; unavailable HSPCA source files are reported instead of importing invented geometry.
The populated Leica import review remains readable in Light and Dark themes.
Discovery, layout previews, database switching and import inspection leave source databases, file inventory and the active project unchanged.
leica_project_browser_ui.platform: Linux Chromium/software WebGL; production HTTP. Synthetic observed Leica SQLite schema, no measured point buffers.

scenarios: Ctrl-select two setups; right-click preserves both and reviews exactly those two, excluding the intermediate registered setup.
A real full-density selected merge publishes one independent, named cloud using saved rigid poses; original files are unchanged.
Undo and Redo restore the whole selected merge atomically without rewriting point caches.
Unregistered/disconnected setups do not offer the registered merge command.
Open Project lists actual saved titles, dates, storage sizes and thumbnails; inspecting a project does not replace the live workspace.
The isolated WebGL project overview renders real saved point geometry in both application themes.
Name search filters cards; single-click 3D preview supports orbit, zoom, plan, elevation and Fit without opening the project.
An older UUID-named snapshot acquires a bounded local point overview without resaving or changing source data.
A late project-preview response cannot replace the more recently selected project.
Browsing a folder reads project titles inside portable files. Older portable files explicitly show bounds instead of claiming a measured point preview.
Open project uses the existing checked save/recovery workflow and opens the chosen named project.
Repeated open/close cycles release preview data and reuse one isolated graphics context; source XYZ stays byte-identical.
An empty current catalogue still offers folder browsing and a clear empty preview; no local named save is required first.
project_browser_ui.platform: Linux Chromium/software WebGL; production HTTP, source files, Undo, portable projects. Synthetic geometry.

dark theme: inspected 29 production dialogs and 480 visible text/control colour pairs.
Dark appearance persists across reload and uses the modern shared surface palette.
The header appearance control changes and saves the theme through the existing preference system.
Real cleaning output: retained/excluded cards, statistics and selected magenta rows remain readable in dark mode.
dark detached review receives shared styles and keeps text/background contrast.
light detached review receives shared styles and keeps text/background contrast.
Individual scan-colour controls use the same modern dialog theme.
modern_workspace_ui.platform: Linux Chromium/software WebGL, production HTTP and real cleaning review. Detached-window transport is controlled; native WebView2 is not executed.

scenarios: Opening an old project places the completed registered cloud and cleaned tunnel outside the 16-setup source bundle.
Bundle deletion review selects only the 16 source setups and explicitly identifies the registered cloud being kept.
Confirmed source-bundle deletion retains both full clouds and the cleaned tunnel edit mask byte for byte.
Workspace reload and named saved-project manifest retain the two independent cloud items after source removal.
Explicitly selecting the registered result still permits its own separate reviewed deletion.
bundle_independence_ui.platform: Linux Chromium/software WebGL; real API, 16 synthetic setups, saved cloud files and retained-point mask.

scenarios: Save shows the real data root, free space, pending project-record folder and native reveal action
Fast named Save writes a named record and Save As displays its existing path
Cancelling the file chooser leaves the working project and destination intact
Save in uses the picker, writes one complete portable copy at the destination, and displays the matching receipt
Declining overwrite retains the previous portable copy byte for byte
With no desktop chooser, entering an absolute destination saves a portable copy
Storage manager shows the data folder and project record

scenarios: Current project guarded in the picker. Single retired project preview counts only its owned cache.
Cancel at review preserves the old project record and its exclusive output.
Unreadable saved metadata blocks a previously reviewed destructive operation.
Equal-byte replacement of the reviewed orphan set requires a new review and removes nothing.
Confirmed multi-project removal quarantines the old-only union once and preserves shared/live/undo/recovery files and protected or unknown inputs byte-for-byte.
Reviewed unreferenced-data cleanup removes exactly the generated orphan. The active project, portable copy, executable, original input, unrelated folder/file, hard link and symlink survive.

real_leica_metadata.note: Previously supplied Leica metadata was inspected read-only. No measured HSPCA point buffers or project catalogue titles were available. Site-map labels are not claimed as the original project titles.

safeguards: Never infer a project title from a UUID, setup, asset, report or workspace name.
Adjacent catalogue titles require the same project GUID.
Site-map fallback labelled; multiple database snapshots require a choice.
Read-only immutable metadata; pending journal changes refused; no point-buffer reads for Leica layout.
Metadata revision guard and late-response selection guard.
Browsing and import inspection leave source inventory and the active workspace unchanged.
limitations: Only the observed Leica SQLite setup schema and explicit title fields are supported.
The previously supplied files expose site-map labels, not original project titles.
No measured HSPCA point buffers accompanied the real metadata samples.
Native Windows/WebView2 and the latest screenshot project were not executed here.
